prediction_question: For a given country of residence, will short-term visitor arrivals to Australia in the first month not yet published (the month after the latest OAD release) fall short of the same calendar month one year earlier?
prediction_time: The publication instant of the ABS Overseas Arrivals and Departures (OAD) release for reference month M, which lands about six weeks after month end (max observed lag 43 days; releases observed 13/10/2026 for Aug 2026, 11/09/2026 for Jul 2026, 12/06/2026 for Apr 2026, all 11:30am local). Features are the published series values for months <= M only; the target month M+1 is unpublished at that instant (it is released ~43 days after its own month end).
target_definition: Binary YoY direction: OBS_VALUE for (CAT_TRAVELLER=06 visitors arriving, COUNTRY_RESID=C, month M+1) < OBS_VALUE for (same series, month M-11). Label source columns: the target month's OBS_VALUE and the year-earlier OBS_VALUE; both excluded from shipped features.

split_strategy: Temporal thirds on the monthly panel of 77 countries x 2 traveller categories: candidate partition train 1991-2014 / eval 2015-2019 / holdout 2022-2026 (2020-2021 excluded as pandemic extremes or optionally folded into train; construction decides and documents). Direction labels are computed per country-series; thresholds are not needed (label is a sign, not a level).

Shipped visitor-series panel: train 19,071 rows / 6,668 positives (34.96%) / 310 flat / 275 distinct positive months (target months 1992-02..2014-12); eval 4,140 / 1,204 (29.08%) / 44 flat / 60 months (2015-01..2019-12); holdout 3,920 / 768 (19.59%) / 72 flat / 45 months (2022-01..2026-08). Eligibility accounted: 224 insufficient_history, 10 unobserved_target, 1,662 pandemic-excluded target months 2020-01..2021-12 (up 494 / down 1,085 / flat 83; 2020 alone: down 766 / up 59 / flat 3), 70 live-month rows scorable the day the next release lands. Known-event fixtures asserted in-build on the shipped series: 2020 border closure down-share 0.9251 (>= 0.75), 2022 reopening up-share 0.9774 (>= 0.75). Reference baselines measured on the written rows (train-estimated tables): persistence (YoY sign observed at M) eval AUC 0.3647 / holdout 0.2256 - persistence is ANTI-correlated with the label in both windows, so the task is a mean-reversion + seasonality problem, not a persistence problem (the nhs-ae defect does not apply here); identity-only (country) 0.5720 / 0.5317; calendar-only (country x calendar month) 0.5501 / 0.5364. Prevalence drift across splits (34.96% -> 29.08% -> 19.59% positives) is the documented phenomenon property (post-2022 recovery boom). reference_baselines.verdict: TRIAD COMPLETE on identical eval rows: persistence (YoY sign at M) 0.3647 < calendar-only (country x cal-month, train-estimated) 0.5501 < identity-only (country) 0.5720 < full model (runner contract) 0.6219. Persistence is ANTI-correlated with the label (0.36 eval / 0.23 holdout), so this is a mean-reversion + seasonality task, not a persistence task - the nhs-ae defect cannot occur. The model clears the calendar-only reference by +0.0718 eval AUC and the identity-only reference by +0.0499: real learned signal beyond seasonality and country identity. Prevalence drift (34.96% train -> 29.08% eval -> 19.59% holdout positives) is the documented post-2022 recovery boom.
